solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, one light wrong at 44 down, 52 across); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 52 across, corrected here

entries.clue: A youngster joining teams that may need dressing (4,5)

indicatorNotes.joining: to join something is to attach yourself to it, so the youngster attaches to the end of the teams

annotation.surface: A young footballer signing up with clubs that need kitting out.
annotation.walkthrough: Dressing in the surface is a team kit; in the answer it is salad dressing. The clue reads youngster first, but the teams come first in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: oil and vinegar are poured over salads, so a dish described as needing dressing points to a salad.

entries.clue: Popular break in very old country (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the popular break is placed in the old word, so it goes inside

blocks.note: sore is an old word for very, as in 'sore afraid'

annotation.surface: A popular holiday taken in some ancient land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very old' looks like ancient, but it asks for an archaic word meaning very, as in the Bible's 'sore afraid'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the island city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula is a sovereign country.

entries.clue: Lovely girl, almost a certain age, grabbing newspaperman to gossip maliciously (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite, so THIRTY stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.grabbing: to grab is to seize and hold, so the age word holds the newspaperman inside it

annotation.surface: A catty remark about an attractive woman nearly thirty who has snared a journalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A certain age' is thirty here, nearly all of it; the editor slips in after its first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: dirt is scandal and to dish is to serve it out, so the phrase means spreading malicious gossip.

entries.clue: First to leave during a little rain break (5)

indicatorNotes.First: the first of a word is its opening letter, so take only the L of 'leave'
indicatorNotes.during: during means within the time of, so the letter goes inside the rain word

annotation.surface: Someone heading home first when a shower threatens a holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First to leave' reads like the earliest guest to go; it is just one letter of leave.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a crack or a fracture in something is a break.

entries.clue: Work at the opera house, struggling to walk, drinking endless tea (2,6)

indicatorNotes.drinking: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so LAME takes the tea into it
indicatorNotes.endless: without an end, so BOHEA loses its last letter

blocks.note: BOHEA, a black China tea, without its end

annotation.surface: An opera-house worker hobbling about, sipping at tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a noun, an opera, not a job. Bohea is an old name for a black China tea, an unusual word worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Puccini's opera about poor artists in Paris is one work staged at opera houses.

entries.clue: Foolishly loving pet, possibly with metal implant (6)

indicatorNotes.implant: an implant is something put inside a body, so the metal goes inside the pet

blocks.note: a dog is one kind of pet
tin, a metal, planted inside DOG

annotation.surface: An owner besotted with a pet that has had a metal pin fitted at the vet's.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the pet as an example, so any common pet could be meant; the metal has to fit inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to dote on someone is to love them to a foolish, uncritical degree.

entries.clue: One highlighting item checked for errors made impervious to attack (13)

blocks.note: a bullet point highlights an item in a list

annotation.surface: An editor's report on a document whose highlighted points have been checked for mistakes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface lives in a word processor; the bullet turns out to be the other kind once the proofing joins it.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal sense stretched: something made proof against gunfire has been made safe from attack.

entries.clue: Arab’s vital struggle for capital (10)

indicatorNotes.struggle: a struggle is a wrestling match, and the letters wrestle into a new order

annotation.surface: A news line about an Arab fighter's crucial battle for a capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Arab’s' is ignored, so its S joins the fodder. The capital is Slovakia's.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Slovakia's seat of government on the Danube is a national capital.

entries.clue: Displeased, releases two examples of these tenants (12)

blocks.note: look at the spelling: disp-LEASE-d, re-LEASE-s
each word holds a lease inside it

annotation.surface: A cross landlord lets go of two of his tenants.
annotation.walkthrough: The first two words are not meant as meanings at all: look at their spelling, each has LEASE inside it, so both are holders of a lease.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who hold property on a lease from a landlord are tenants.

entries.clue: Cause a jam in three directions and peer round (7)

indicatorNotes.round: to go round something is to encircle it, so the peer surrounds the directions

annotation.surface: Traffic snarled up at a three-way junction, a nobleman looking about him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look; it is a nobleman, split after his first letter around the three compass points.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a snarl is a tangle or jam, and to ensnarl is to cause one.

entries.clue: Genuine part that cannot be reduced (6,8)

annotation.definition: Genuine part that cannot be reduced

blocks.note: genuine and part each have an arithmetic-flavoured synonym
something smaller than one whole, so it cannot be cut down to a whole number plus a remainder

annotation.surface: A mechanic insisting on a genuine spare part, not a cheaper cut-down copy.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as garage talk, 'genuine part' is an original spare. In arithmetic, a proper fraction such as 3/4 is less than one, unlike 7/4, which can be brought down to 1¾.
annotation.definitionFit: A mathematical term: genuine = proper and a part = a fraction, and such a fraction, below one, has no whole-number part to reduce to.

entries.clue: Service book is unremarkable, with one line changed for another (7)

indicatorNotes.changed for another: to change one thing for another is to swap it, so one line is exchanged for a different line

blocks.note: RY (railway, a line) is swapped for L (line)

annotation.surface: A dull hymn book, with one line swapped around by the editor.
annotation.walkthrough: RY is the railway abbreviation and L is line; both are lines, so one line is changed for another.
annotation.definitionFit: A church term: this is the book setting out the order of services, especially ordinations.

entries.clue: One fired for failing challenge (6,2,3)

indicatorNotes.failing: something failing is breaking down, and the letters break down into a new order

annotation.surface: A worker sacked for poor performance.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about being dismissed from a job; 'fired' is only letters, and the answer is a sentry's cry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a sentry's shouted demand to someone approaching in the dark is a challenge.

entries.clue: Toy, about 67 cents? (4)

indicatorNotes.about 67 cents?: 67 cents is roughly two-thirds of a dollar, so keep two-thirds of the word DOLLAR

blocks.note: the first four of DOLLAR's six letters

annotation.surface: A price tag on a toy.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark says to take the fraction literally: two-thirds of the currency's name, not its value.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a child's figure of a person, played with, is a toy.

entries.clue: Space explorers left as the hooter sounds (5)

annotation.definitionNote: an adverbial phrase for an adjective: something nasal sounds the way a nose does
annotation.surface: Astronauts departing as the launch siren goes off.
annotation.walkthrough: The hooter in the surface is a siren; in the answer it is British slang for the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: a hooter is a nose, and a voice through the nose has this quality.

entries.clue: Handing over deeds, live alone looking seriously at first housing board (9)

indicatorNotes.at first: at first means at the start, so take the opening letter of each of the three words
indicatorNotes.housing: to house something is to give it a home inside, so BE…ALS holds the board

blocks.note: a tray is a flat board
first letters of alone, looking, seriously

annotation.surface: Signing over property deeds while living alone and taking it all very seriously.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handing over' sounds like conveyancing; the deeds are acts of handing someone over to an enemy.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: acts of treachery hand people over to their enemies, as Judas did.

entries.clue: Force bishop to visit aged and sick (3,4)

indicatorNotes.to visit: a visitor comes into a place, so the bishop comes in between the two states

annotation.surface: A bishop being made to call on the old and infirm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb; it is the police force. The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: the police force is known informally by this name.

entries.clue: Proverbial advice to surgeon not to delay closing incision? (1,6,2,4,5,4)

annotation.answer: A STITCH IN TIME SAVES NINE

blocks.clueFragment: to surgeon not to delay closing incision?
blocks.note: the saying read literally, as a surgeon's sewing

annotation.surface: A theatre sister telling a surgeon to sew up the wound promptly.
annotation.walkthrough: The proverb is about fixing small problems early; the clue takes its stitch literally, in an operating theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: A proverb: the saying urges prompt small repairs to prevent bigger ones, which is advice.

entries.clue: Set out, stripped of all devices, you might say? (8)

blocks.clueFragment: stripped of all devices, you might say?
blocks.note: devices = ploys, tricks; a made-up word for having them removed

annotation.surface: Someone sent off with every gadget taken from them.
annotation.walkthrough: Ploys are devices in the sense of tricks, and 'de-' strips them away, so 'de-ployed' is a made-up word the question mark owns up to.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: troops placed in position for action have been set out.

entries.clue: Work that’s better-paid perhaps, but not all at once (8)

blocks.note: extra hours, often at a higher rate

annotation.surface: A worker weighing up better-paid extra shifts that do not come all at once.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two, OVER TIME, for the second sense: spread out, not in one go.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: extra hours beyond the normal day, often paid at a higher rate; and, as two words, gradually.

entries.clue: Drink to the ladies, say, standing to embrace daughter that grows up in the woods (9)

annotation.definition: that grows up in the woods

indicatorNotes.standing: to stand is to be upright, and in a down clue an upright word reads bottom to top
indicatorNotes.to embrace: an embrace wraps arms round someone, so TOAST wraps round the daughter

blocks.note: to drink to someone is to toast them
the ladies is one example of a loo, a toilet

annotation.surface: A father raising a glass to the women and hugging his grown-up daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The ladies' is the women's toilet, a British sense; 'say' marks it as one kind of loo.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: this fungus springs up from the forest floor.

entries.clue: Viola plays in this a lot, changing opening briefly (4,4)

indicatorNotes.changing: changing means altering, so the letters of A LOT alter their order
indicatorNotes.briefly: briefly means in short, so CLEFT is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: a cleft is an opening; cut short

annotation.surface: A string player whose part keeps changing its key at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Viola' reads as a woman's name as much as an instrument; the instrument's music is written on a stave with its own clef.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical fact: viola music is written with the C clef on the middle line, which is what this clef is.

entries.clue: Not compact, igloo seems in need of trimming (5)

indicatorNotes.in need of trimming: trimming cuts off the edges, so the ends of 'igloo seems' come away

blocks.note: drop the first two and last two letters

annotation.surface: An igloo whose snow blocks are loosely packed and need tidying.
annotation.walkthrough: The trimming takes the ends off both words together, as one string of letters, not each word separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something loosely packed, not dense or tight, is not compact.

entries.clue: A bit of relaxation disturbed in the middle in largely rural area (8)

indicatorNotes.disturbed in the middle: to disturb something is to move it out of place, so the middle letters of REST move

blocks.note: REST with its middle two letters swapped

annotation.surface: A short break interrupted halfway through, somewhere out in the countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: A bit of relaxation is a single phrase, one letter-swap from the answer. Somerset is a mostly rural county in the south-west of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: this south-western English county is mostly farmland, levels and moor.

entries.clue: Pilgrim returning to follow the Andalusian prophet (6)

indicatorNotes.returning: to return is to go back, so the pilgrim word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.to follow: what follows comes after, so the pilgrim goes after the Spanish word

blocks.note: a haji has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

annotation.surface: A pilgrim heading home behind a Spanish holy man.
annotation.walkthrough: Andalusia is in southern Spain, so 'the Andalusian' is the Spanish word for the.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Old Testament figure taken up in a chariot of fire is one prophet.

entries.clue: Caught men recording crow (6)

annotation.surface: Birdwatchers filming a crow they have caught.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Men' means soldiers here: the other ranks, as opposed to officers.
annotation.definitionFit: A family name: the crow belongs to the bird family Corvidae, and any member of it goes by this name.

entries.clue: Suffering acute flu, parking quantity of drink (9)

indicatorNotes.Suffering: something suffering is in a bad way, and the letters are knocked out of shape
indicatorNotes.parking: parking is abbreviated P, and the mixture parks that letter inside itself

blocks.note: P = parking, taken into the mix

annotation.surface: A patient with bad flu trying to take in a hot drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the remedy; the answer is simply how much the cup holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A measure: as much as a small cup holds is a quantity of drink.

entries.clue: Rugby team said to suffer defeat? (8)

indicatorNotes.said: something said is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

annotation.surface: A rugby side tipped to be beaten.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair warning: the French club is famous, and in fact a winning one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stade Toulousain, the club of the southern French city, is one rugby team.

entries.clue: Be the most loquacious, to the ultimate degree (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is an adjective (or noun, as in 'to the uttermost'); the definition is a phrase

blocks.note: a joke sense: speak more than anyone

annotation.surface: Talk the most, to the greatest possible extent.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half only works split in two, as a verb and an adverb: the chattiest person is the one who says the most.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: utmost, extreme; and, split as two words, to speak more than anyone else.

entries.clue: Frightful hag with deformity, or quite the opposite? (5,9)

indicatorNotes.Frightful: frightful means dreadful, and the letters are in a dreadful state that needs rearranging

annotation.surface: A witch in a fairy tale, deformed and ugly, or maybe not.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the wordplay: the opposite of a frightful, deformed hag is the kindly helper of Cinderella.
annotation.definitionFit: A contrast definition: the benevolent magical helper of fairy tales is the reverse of a frightful hag.

entries.clue: In a while employing dull-witted (but not British) idler (5-5)

indicatorNotes.employing: to employ something is to take it on, so LATER takes the middle word into itself
indicatorNotes.but not: 'but not' excludes something, so OBTUSE goes without its B

annotation.surface: Someone planning to hire a slow-witted foreigner as a layabout.
annotation.walkthrough: The dull-witted word goes in after LATER's first letter. The lotus-eaters of Homer's Odyssey lived in dreamy idleness.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary allusion: Homer's lotus-eaters lazed in drugged contentment, so the term means a dreamy idler.

entries.clue: Edges round county briefly, having this to face? (3,5)

indicatorNotes.round: to go round is to surround, so the edges wrap round the county
indicatorNotes.briefly: briefly means in short, so the county appears in its short form

blocks.note: Glos is short for Gloucestershire, an English county

annotation.surface: Someone skirting round a county, with this to face at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face' is a verb in the surface; in the definition it is the face the gloss goes on.
annotation.definitionFit: A cosmetic applied to the face: the question mark flags the pun on 'face' as a verb.

entries.clue: Foreign woman united with religious brother (4)

indicatorNotes.with: with means together, so the two pieces stand side by side

blocks.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar
U = united, as in team names

annotation.surface: A woman from abroad marrying a monk.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads united first, but the brother comes first in the answer; 'with' sets no order.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign word: German for a married woman or wife, so a woman from abroad.

entries.clue: China, maybe needing time to replace leader, becomes unstable (7)

indicatorNotes.needing: to need something is to require it, so the china word requires a T
indicatorNotes.to replace leader: to replace is to take the place of, so T takes the place of the first letter

blocks.note: china is one kind of pottery

annotation.surface: A report that China, needing a new head of state, is wobbling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country; it is crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shaky on one's feet, inclined to wobble, is unstable.

entries.clue: After love, contraceptive to alleviate unwelcome prospect (5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.After: after means following, so the contraceptive comes after the endearment

blocks.note: sugar, like love, is a term of endearment

annotation.surface: Contraception taken after lovemaking to ease the worry of a pregnancy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love' in the surface is lovemaking; in the wordplay it is a pet name, and there is another sweet one.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: coating a bitter pill makes it easier to swallow, so the phrase means softening something unwelcome.

entries.clue: Knock about football at last, next to our room for games? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so the knock reads backwards
indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of football
indicatorNotes.next to: next to means beside, so the pieces sit side by side

annotation.surface: Kicking a football about indoors at last, beside the family games room.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition: parlour games are named after the room they were played in.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: the old-fashioned sitting room gave its name to parlour games.

entries.clue: Protest as broadcast torments ear (11)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so the letters are scattered

annotation.surface: Complaining that a noisy broadcast is hurting the listener's ears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio, which suits the ear in the surface, but it is the sower's word for scattering.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to make a forceful objection is to protest.

entries.clue: Rejected objections, small part remaining (4)

indicatorNotes.Rejected: to reject is literally to throw back, so the word is thrown back and reads backwards

blocks.note: buts = objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

annotation.surface: A committee throws out the complaints, leaving only a small section.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rejected objections' reads like a ruling in a meeting; it is the objections word turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the counterfoil of a ticket or the end of a candle is the small part left.

entries.clue: Keep out of sight in Togo, it is suggested (2,2,6)

blocks.note: the country's name is two small words swapped, and a country is ground

annotation.surface: Advice to lie low while in the West African state of Togo.
annotation.walkthrough: Togo reads as the country, but its letters say GO TO with the halves switched; 'it is suggested' admits this is a hint, not a strict parse.
annotation.definitionFit: A hunting idiom: a fox bolting into its earth hides, so the phrase means to keep out of sight.

entries.clue: Assuming responsibility for dangerous piece of driving (11)

blocks.note: taking on a task or duty
passing another car on the inside lane

annotation.surface: Admitting blame for a reckless manoeuvre on the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage, undertaking is overtaking on the wrong side, the inside lane, which is dangerous.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: taking on a duty; and, in British driving slang, passing on the inside.

entries.clue: On good terms always? Fancy that (4,1,5)

blocks.note: well in with someone = on good terms

annotation.surface: A surprised reaction to hearing two people are firm friends for good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that' is an exclamation of surprise, not a verb about liking something.
annotation.definitionFit: Two exclamations of surprise used interchangeably in British speech.

entries.clue: Escape hole in gentle radiation (9)

blocks.note: on the lam = on the run, escaping
a hole = a plight, a fix

annotation.surface: A way out of a pit, lit by a soft glow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hole' is a figurative one: being in a hole is being in a tight spot.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the soft glow from a lamp is light radiated gently.

entries.clue: Reluctant potholers initially going east (6)

indicatorNotes.initially going: going means leaving, so the initial letter leaves

annotation.surface: Nervous cave explorers setting off eastwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks as if it takes the P of potholers; with 'going' it removes the first letter of their synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being set against doing something is being reluctant.

entries.clue: No way I compete up front in such skiing (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is an adjective; 'such' stands for it in front of 'skiing'

indicatorNotes.up front: up front means at the start, so only the first letter of compete

annotation.surface: A skier refusing to race in the front row of a cross-country event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like a refusal; it splits into the word as written and a road.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting term: cross-country skiing, as opposed to downhill Alpine skiing, goes by this name.

entries.clue: Clean home furiously — it may become a different colour (9)

annotation.definition: it may become a different colour

indicatorNotes.furiously: doing something furiously is doing it wildly, so the letters are thrown about

annotation.surface: Scrubbing a house so hard that its paintwork changes shade.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures bleach on paintwork; the thing that changes colour is an animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: this lizard shifts its skin colour to blend in or signal mood.

entries.clue: Moderate line by BBC and others (3,5)

annotation.surface: An editorial policy of moderation shared by the BBC and other broadcasters.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is Latin for the middle way, used in English of a compromise course.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Latin phrase: 'the middle road' is a moderate line between extremes.

entries.clue: A hole in the head is wrong and useless (5)

indicatorNotes.and: and adds one thing to another, so the second piece follows the first

annotation.surface: Someone saying a pointless wrong idea is about as welcome as a hole in the head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A hole in the head' sounds like the idiom for something unwanted; here it is literal, an air cavity in the skull.
annotation.definitionFit: Anatomy taken literally: the air-filled cavities in the skull bones are holes in the head.

entries.clue: Cast off as stage backdrops collapse, just missing the lead (3,4)

indicatorNotes.just missing the lead: to miss something is to be without it, so FAIL is without its leading letter

annotation.surface: Scenery falling down in a theatre, the star only just escaping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The lead' sounds like the leading actor; it is the leading letter of the collapse word.
annotation.definitionFit: A sailing sense: to cast off the mooring lines is to begin a voyage.

entries.clue: Regularly keeping home neat, ultimately with elegance (8)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so DAILY holds the other letters
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of neat

annotation.surface: Someone tidying the house every day, and stylishly with it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' usually picks alternate letters; here it is simply a synonym, every day.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something delicately and prettily is doing it with elegance.

entries.clue: Tip from Bow: not polite to barge in (7)

indicatorNotes.from Bow: said as a Cockney from Bow would, dropping the H

annotation.surface: A warning, East End style, that it is rude to push in.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, where Cockneys traditionally drop their Hs, so a hint becomes 'int.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to push in where one is not wanted is to barge in.

entries.clue: Queen playing Act I or IV (8)

indicatorNotes.playing: playing a part means acting a role, and the letters take on a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An actress cast as the queen in the first or fourth act of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: The Roman numerals look like stage directions; they are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Britain's long-reigning 19th-century monarch is one queen.

entries.clue: Departs on journey, getting a lift; I’m grateful to have that good military ID (3,3)

indicatorNotes.getting a lift: a lift raises something, and in a down clue a raised word reads upward

annotation.surface: A hitch-hiker thanking a driver for a lift, with a soldier's ID round their neck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is everyday British for thank you, which is all 'I'm grateful' asks for.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: soldiers wear a metal identity disc on a chain, nicknamed for a pet's collar tag.

entries.clue: Same housing estate often trashed in annual report (5,2,3,5,7)

indicatorNotes.trashed: something trashed has been wrecked, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

annotation.surface: A council report noting the same estate is regularly vandalised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like a container indicator; it is part of the fodder, all four words of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the US President's yearly address to Congress reports on the nation.

entries.clue: Sudden applause greeting shortened opening of opera (5)

indicatorNotes.shortened: shortened means made shorter, so the greeting loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.opening of: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of opera

annotation.surface: An audience bursting into applause at the curtailed overture of an opera.
annotation.walkthrough: Salve is a Latin greeting, 'hail', as carved on Roman doorsteps.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a volley of gunfire lends its name to a sudden burst of applause.

entries.clue: Eject from small seat (4)

blocks.note: a pew is a church seat

annotation.surface: Being thrown off a little chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seat' suggests a chair; the one wanted is the bench in a church.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to gush or throw something out forcefully is to eject it.

entries.clue: Not that good an effort in Boat Race, we are told? Say “Tut!” (7)

indicatorNotes.we are told: what we are told we hear, so the phrase is heard, not read

blocks.clueFragment: Not that good an effort in Boat Race
blocks.note: a fair oar = a middling rower in the Boat Race

annotation.surface: A spectator tutting at a mediocre crew in the Oxford–Cambridge Boat Race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tut' is not a tut of disapproval but Tutankhamun, and 'say' marks him as an example. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: King Tut, the boy king of ancient Egypt, was one of its rulers.

entries.clue: Not expected in concert to introduce one new verse (9)

indicatorNotes.to introduce: to introduce is to bring in, so the in-concert word brings the letters inside it

blocks.note: I = one, N = new, V = verse

annotation.surface: A surprise encore where the band brings in an extra verse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In concert' sounds like live music; it means acting together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a guest who turns up without being asked is not expected.

entries.clue: Learning about current in river abroad (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the learning word goes around the current

annotation.surface: Studying the currents of a foreign river.
annotation.walkthrough: The water sense of 'current' fits the river surface, but here it is the electrical symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: France's longest river, flowing past the châteaux, is a river abroad from a British view.

entries.clue: Unscrupulous sort of bicycle salesman? (7-6)

annotation.surface: A shady bike seller.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a dealer in wheels, a bicycle salesman.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal term: a shrewd operator who makes deals by fair means or foul is an unscrupulous sort.

entries.clue: Girl, avoiding Irish, meeting a Welshman where he might have lived? (9)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so the word GIRL keeps clear of IR
indicatorNotes.meeting: things that meet come together, so the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: the word GIRL without IR, short for Irish

annotation.surface: A girl dodging an Irish suitor for a Welsh one, and wondering where he came from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Girl' is not a synonym here: it is the word itself losing two letters. The answer is a historic county of south Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition referring back: a Welshman might well have lived in this south Wales county.
